# The reasons

The most remarkable chapter of the 1446 book is the one that explains
*why*: why ㄱ (*g*) is shaped like the root of a tongue blocking a throat, why
the vowels build from three primitives. For five hundred years that
chapter was lost, and the world had the letters but not the reasons; only
in 1940 did a surviving copy resurface. The letters worked the whole time.
But a system whose reasons are lost cannot be extended, only used.

This part is gog's reasons, published with the package on purpose. It
states the nine laws the package never breaks, and the shortcut each law
exists to refuse. It says why the engine refuses what it refuses, and why
every refusal comes with a direction. None of it is required to *use*
gog: Parts I to IV never depend on it. It is here for the moment you want to know why the
grammar is shaped the way it is, or want to predict what it will do in a
case no chapter covers.

The laws all refuse the same thing, and it has a name: the expert's
shortcut, the saved keystroke that takes a rule away from the beginner.
